title: ReLMem: Learning Recurrent Memory for Longitudinal EHR Modeling
abstract: arXiv:2609.37587v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) modeling requires integrating new visits with an expanding patient history. Yet the continual accumulation of clinical information imposes increasing computational and memory costs on large language models (LLMs) when they process and retain complete patient histories. A practical alternative is visit-wise recurrent compression, which incorporates each incoming visit into a compact, continually updated patient memory. However, under a fixed memory budget, successive updates must integrate new information without progressively losing critical historical evidence needed to subsequent tasks. To address this challenge, we introduce Recurrent Longitudinal Memory (ReLMem), a framework that learns to maintain fixed-capacity patient memory for efficient downstream prediction with a frozen LLM. translated_title: ReLMem：学习用于纵向电子健康记录建模的循环记忆
translated_abstract: 纵向电子健康记录（EHR）建模需要将新的就诊信息与不断扩展的患者病史进行整合。然而，临床信息的持续累积使大语言模型（LLMs）在处理和保留完整患者病史时面临日益增加的计算和内存开销。一种实用的替代方案是按就诊进行循环压缩，即将每次新到的就诊信息纳入一个紧凑且持续更新的患者记忆中。然而，在固定的记忆预算下，连续的更新必须在整合新信息的同时，避免逐步丢失后续任务所需的关键历史证据。为应对这一挑战，我们提出了循环纵向记忆框架ReLMem，该框架学习维护固定容量的患者记忆，从而在冻结的大语言模型上实现高效的下游预测。ReLMem为该大语言模型配备轻量级压缩适配器，以循环方式利用其之前的记忆来更新……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出了ReLMem框架，通过轻量级压缩适配器循环地维护固定容量的患者记忆，使冻结的大语言模型能够高效整合不断增长的纵向EHR数据，同时避免丢失后续任务所需的关键历史信息。
en_tdlr: ReLMem learns to maintain fixed-capacity patient memory through lightweight compression adapters, enabling a frozen LLM to efficiently integrate growing longitudinal EHR data without progressively losing critical historical evidence for downstream predictions.
